definition: Scrutinize means to examine something closely and critically.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word scrutinize. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know scrutinize should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: New parents scrutinize every label in the baby aisle, hunting the one ingredient the doctor warned them about.
A glance is the weakest look there is — a half-second sweep that registers almost nothing, far milder than scrutinize.
Inspecting goes further than glancing, checking a thing over with real care, but it is still gentler than scrutinize, which hunts for what is wrong.
Dissect goes further than scrutinize: scrutiny questions every detail from the outside, while dissection takes the thing apart piece by piece.

Examine is the neutral word for a careful look — a doctor examines a knee, a teacher examines an essay — thorough, but with no suspicion in it. Scrutinize sharpens the same act: the looker is hunting for something wrong and questions every detail until it gives.

To vet is to check a person or plan for hidden problems before approval — the look ends in a yes or a no. Scrutinize carries no gate to pass: you can scrutinize anything, at any point, whenever suspicion demands it. Vetting guards a door; scrutiny hunts a flaw.
